title: Machines with nonnegative work heads
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, let $f$ map words over $\Gamma$ to words over $\Gamma$, and let $T\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. If $M$ computes $f$ in time $T$, then there are a finite alphabet $\Gamma'$ with decidable equality, an injection $e\colon\Gamma\hookrightarrow\Gamma'$, a finite Turing machine $M'$ over $\Gamma'$, and a constant $c\in\mathbb N$ such that every work head of $M'$ stays at a nonnegative cell throughout every initialized run, $M'$ has the same number of work tapes as $M$, and $M'$ computes $f$ on symbolwise encoded inputs via $e$ within $c(T(n)+1)$ steps on inputs of length $n$.
replaced:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $M$ be a multi-tape
Turing machine over $\Gamma$, and suppose $M$ computes a function
$f \colon \Gamma^* \to \Gamma^*$ within a time bound $T \colon \bbn \to \bbn$.
Then there exist a finite alphabet $\Gamma'$ with decidable equality, an injection
$e \colon \Gamma \hookrightarrow \Gamma'$, a machine $M'$ over $\Gamma'$, and a
constant $c \in \bbn$ such that: in every initialized run of $M'$ no work head ever
visits a negative cell, $M'$ has the same number of work tapes as $M$, and $M'$
computes $f$ through the embedding $e$ within the time bound
$n \mapsto c \cdot (T(n) + 1)$.
